title: Psalms Chapter 9 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 9 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 9 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 9.

questions.question: Who is the psalm attributed to in Psalms 9?
questions.explanation: The psalm is explicitly stated as 'A Psalm of David' in verse 1.

questions.question: What does David intend to do with his whole heart according to Psalms 9?
questions.explanation: David says, 'I will praise thee, O LORD, with my whole heart' in verse 1.

questions.question: According to Psalms 9:2, what will David do in addition to praising the LORD?
questions.explanation: David states, 'I will sing praise to thy name, O thou most High' in verse 2.

questions.question: True or False: David will rejoice in the presence of the LORD according to Psalms 9.
questions.explanation: David expresses his joy in verse 2, stating 'I will be glad and rejoice in thee.'

questions.question: What happens to David's enemies when they are turned back according to Psalms 9:3?
questions.explanation: Verse 3 says, 'When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish at thy presence.'

questions.question: What does the LORD maintain according to Psalms 9:4?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For thou hast maintained my right and my cause' in verse 4.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD is described as judging with wickedness in Psalms 9.
questions.explanation: The verse states that the LORD judges 'right' in verse 4, indicating righteousness, not wickedness.

questions.question: What has the LORD done to the heathen according to Psalms 9:5?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states, 'Thou hast rebuked the heathen.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 9:7, what has the LORD prepared for judgment?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'he hath prepared his throne for judgment' in verse 7.

questions.question: True or False: The memorial of the cities destroyed by the enemy still remains according to Psalms 9:6.
questions.explanation: The verse states that 'their memorial is perished with them,' indicating that it does not remain.

questions.question: In what manner will the LORD judge the world according to Psalms 9:8?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'he shall judge the world in righteousness' in verse 8.

questions.question: In Psalms 9, what comes first according to the chapter's events?
questions.explanation: The first instruction given in the chapter is to 'praise thee, O LORD' in verse 1.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 9 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 9 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:8 say about God's judgment?
options: He shall judge the world in righteousness
He shall judge the world in anger
He shall judge the world unfairly
He shall not judge the world
questions.correctAnswer: He shall judge the world in righteousness
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:8 states that God shall judge the world in righteousness, indicating His just and fair nature in administering justice.

questions.question: According to Psalms 9:9, who will find refuge in the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:9 declares that the LORD will be a refuge for the oppressed, highlighting His care for those in need.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:10 promise to those who know God's name?
options: They will put their trust in God
questions.correctAnswer: They will put their trust in God
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:10 states that those who know God's name will put their trust in Him, as He has not forsaken those who seek Him.

questions.question: What is the significance of singing praises to the LORD as mentioned in Psalms 9:11?
options: To declare God's doings among the people
questions.correctAnswer: To declare God's doings among the people
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:11 encourages singing praises to the LORD to declare His works among the people, emphasizing the importance of sharing God's greatness.

questions.question: According to Psalms 9:12, what does God remember during His inquisition for blood?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:12 states that God remembers the cry of the humble when He makes inquisition for blood, highlighting His attentiveness to the lowly.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:13 ask God to do in response to trouble?
options: Consider the trouble and have mercy
questions.correctAnswer: Consider the trouble and have mercy
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:13 is a plea for God to have mercy and consider the trouble of the psalmist, indicating a reliance on God's compassion.

questions.question: What does the psalmist express a desire to do in the gates of the daughter of Zion as per Psalms 9:14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:14 expresses the psalmist's desire to show forth all God's praise, demonstrating the importance of public worship and acknowledgment of God's salvation.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 9:15 describes the heathen being successful in their schemes.
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:15 states that the heathen are sunk down in the pit they made, indicating their failure and downfall rather than success.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 9:17 says that the wicked shall be turned into hell.
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:17 explicitly states that the wicked shall be turned into hell, affirming the consequences of rejecting God.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:18 say about the needy?
options: They will be provided for in abundance
They shall not always be forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: They shall not always be forgotten
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:18 assures that the needy shall not always be forgotten, indicating God's promise to remember and act on their behalf.

questions.question: What is the prayer in Psalms 9:19 regarding mankind's position before God?
options: Let man be judged in the sight of God
questions.correctAnswer: Let the heathen be judged in thy sight
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:19 prays for God to let the heathen be judged in His sight, emphasizing the need for divine justice.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:20 ask God to do to the nations?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:20 asks God to put the nations in fear, so they may recognize their limitations and humanity before His power.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 9:16 states that the wicked will be saved from their own actions.
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:16 indicates that the wicked are snared in the work of their own hands, signifying that they cannot escape the consequences of their actions.

questions.question: According to Psalms 9:10, why can those who trust in the LORD feel secure?
options: Because they do not have enemies
Because the LORD has not forsaken them
questions.correctAnswer: Because the LORD has not forsaken them
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:10 reassures that the LORD has not forsaken those who seek Him, providing a basis for trust and security.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 9 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 9.

questions.question: In Psalms 9:15, what happens to the heathen in the pit they have made?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'The heathen are sunk down in the pit that they made: in the net which they hid is their own foot taken,' illustrating the consequences of their own actions.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:18 say about the needy?
options: Their expectation shall not perish forever
questions.correctAnswer: Their expectation shall not perish forever
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'For the needy shall not alway be forgotten: the expectation of the poor shall not perish for ever,' indicating God's ongoing care for the needy.

questions.question: According to Psalms 9:20, what does the psalmist ask the LORD to do regarding man?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Put them in fear, O LORD: that the nations may know themselves to be but men,' highlighting the necessity of humility before God.

questions.question: Which theme is echoed in Psalms 9 regarding God's judgment found in other Scriptures?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:16 states, 'The LORD is known by the judgment which he executeth,' which parallels Romans 2:6, 'Who will render to every man according to his deeds.'

questions.question: In Psalms 9:11, where does the LORD dwell?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Sing praises to the LORD, which dwelleth in Zion,' indicating His chosen dwelling place among His people.

questions.question: What is the significance of the term 'Selah' found in Psalms 9:16 and 9:20?
questions.explanation: The term 'Selah' is often understood as a musical term that signals a pause or interlude in the psalm, allowing reflection on the preceding text.

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 9:4, God judges with bias and favoritism.
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:4 says, 'thou satest in the throne judging right,' emphasizing God's impartiality in His judgment.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:17 indicate will happen to the wicked?
options: They shall be turned into hell
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be turned into hell
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'The wicked shall be turned into hell, and all the nations that forget God,' indicating the fate of the wicked.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 9:10 assures that the LORD forsakes those who seek Him.
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:10 states, 'for thou, LORD, hast not forsaken them that seek thee,' assuring His faithful presence.

questions.question: In Psalms 9:6, what has happened to the cities of the enemy?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'thou hast destroyed cities; their memorial is perished with them,' indicating total destruction.

questions.question: What literary device is used in Psalms 9:10 with the repetition of the phrase 'thou'?
questions.explanation: The repetition of 'thou' at the beginning of phrases emphasizes God's attributes and actions, which is characteristic of anaphora.

questions.question: In Psalms 9:8, how does the LORD execute judgment?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:8 states, 'he shall judge the world in righteousness,' highlighting the just nature of His judgment.

questions.question: According to Psalms 9:12, what does the LORD remember?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'he forgetteth not the cry of the humble,' emphasizing God's attention to the pleas of the lowly.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:3 indicate will happen to the enemies when they are in God's presence?
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'When mine enemies are turned back, they shall fall and perish at thy presence,' showing God's power over adversaries.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 9 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 9 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:1 reveal about the attitude of the psalmist towards God?
options: He will praise God with his whole heart
He will blame God for his troubles
questions.correctAnswer: He will praise God with his whole heart
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses a commitment to praise the Lord wholeheartedly as indicated in Psalms 9:1, emphasizing the importance of sincere worship.

questions.question: According to Psalms 9:2, how does the psalmist respond to God's greatness?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 9:2, the psalmist states, 'I will sing praise to thy name,' showing that he responds to God's greatness with joy and worship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:4 teach about God's role as a judge?
options: He does not judge at all
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:4 indicates that God sits on the throne judging right, affirming His role as a just and righteous judge.

questions.question: What is the psalmist's view of the fate of the wicked as per Psalms 9:5?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:5 states that God has put out the name of the wicked forever, indicating their ultimate destruction and forgetfulness.

questions.question: What assurance does Psalms 9:9 provide for the oppressed?
options: The LORD will be their refuge
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will be their refuge
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:9 assures that the LORD will be a refuge for the oppressed, indicating His protective and caring nature.

questions.question: In Psalms 9:12, what does the psalmist highlight about God's memory?
options: He remembers the cry of the humble
questions.correctAnswer: He remembers the cry of the humble
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:12 emphasizes that God remembers the cry of the humble, illustrating His attentiveness to the needs of the lowly and oppressed.

questions.question: According to Psalms 9:14, what does the psalmist desire to do in the gates of the daughter of Zion?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 9:14, the psalmist expresses his intention to show forth all God's praise in Zion, highlighting the importance of public worship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 9:16 reveal about God's judgment?
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:16 states that the LORD is known by the judgment He executes, affirming His righteous character in administering justice.

questions.question: What fate does Psalms 9:17 describe for the wicked?
options: They shall be turned into hell
questions.correctAnswer: They shall be turned into hell
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:17 clearly states that the wicked shall be turned into hell, emphasizing the seriousness of divine judgment against evil.

questions.question: How does Psalms 9:18 address the needy?
options: They will not always be forgotten
questions.correctAnswer: They will not always be forgotten
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:18 assures that the needy shall not always be forgotten, highlighting God's care and remembrance of the poor.

questions.question: What request does the psalmist make in Psalms 9:19?
options: That the LORD arise and judge man
questions.correctAnswer: That the LORD arise and judge man
questions.explanation: In Psalms 9:19, the psalmist calls upon the LORD to arise and let not man prevail, emphasizing his reliance on God's justice.

questions.question: What does the psalmist mean by 'Let the heathen be judged in thy sight' in Psalms 9:19?
options: The heathen will be judged publicly
questions.correctAnswer: The heathen will be judged publicly
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:19 indicates a desire for the heathen to be judged in God's sight, suggesting a public acknowledgment of God's authority and justice.

questions.question: What combined teaching do Psalms 9:3 and 9:5 convey about God's power over enemies?
options: He turns enemies back and destroys the wicked
questions.correctAnswer: He turns enemies back and destroys the wicked
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:3 states that enemies are turned back, and Psalms 9:5 elaborates that God has destroyed the wicked, showcasing His supreme power over adversaries.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be drawn from Psalms 9:10 and 9:14 regarding trust and salvation?
options: Knowing God's name results in trust and leads to rejoicing in salvation
questions.correctAnswer: Knowing God's name results in trust and leads to rejoicing in salvation
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:10 emphasizes trust in God for those who know His name, while Psalms 9:14 connects this trust to rejoicing in His salvation.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is indifferent to the plight of the oppressed. What does Psalms 9:9-10 actually teach?
options: God is a refuge for the oppressed
God is only concerned with the rich
questions.correctAnswer: God is a refuge for the oppressed
questions.explanation: Psalms 9:9-10 teaches that the LORD is a refuge for the oppressed and that those who know Him will trust in Him, countering the sceptics' claim of indifference.
